status: coverage stress test; not a ranked forecast and not an exhaustive set of likely advances
population: 50 concrete structural or algorithmic breakthrough scenarios selected to probe coverage. Opposite answers to one open question are not systematically counted twice.
interpretation: Direct and consequence mean that a mathematical mapping is provided, conditional on the mapped pair being certified open at the cutoff. They do not certify that the result was still open or guarantee an official score in the draft benchmark. Unsupported means no scored implication is established here, not that no implication could ever exist.

scenarios.eligibility: pending cutoff certification; direct reduction argument supplied

scenarios.title: Polynomial-time graph isomorphism
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: A faster algorithm for this individual language does not imply that NP, SPP or any other roster class collapses. GI is not known complete for those classes.

scenarios.title: Classical polynomial-time integer factoring
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: Factoring is a particular search/function problem. Its efficient solution need not decide every language in NP intersect coNP or BQP.

scenarios.title: Deterministic polynomial-time general polynomial identity testing
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: Known implications include a disjunction: NEXP lacks polynomial-size Boolean circuits OR permanent lacks polynomial-size arithmetic circuits. The second branch need not settle a roster pair.

scenarios.title: Prove the matrix multiplication exponent is two
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: All the algorithms involved remain polynomial time; the roster has no fixed-exponent arithmetic-operation classes.

scenarios.title: Refute SETH with a faster exponential-time SAT algorithm
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: A speedup can refute a quantitative hypothesis while leaving P versus NP and all roster inclusions unresolved. A proof of ETH or SETH would imply NP not contained in P, but refutation need not.

scenarios.title: Truly subquadratic exact edit distance
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: This distinguishes polynomial exponents inside P. Without a separate theorem connecting the speedup to a roster relation, the benchmark awards no point.

scenarios.title: Polynomial-time algorithms for every PPAD search problem
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: PPAD is a class of total search relations, outside this language roster. Solving PPAD-complete Nash problems need not settle any listed language inclusion.

scenarios.title: Separate VP from VNP over characteristic zero
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: Algebraic circuit families are not Boolean decision-language classes. No implication to a scored Boolean pair is supplied by this benchmark.

scenarios.title: Superpolynomial lower bounds for Frege proofs
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: Lower bounds for one proof system do not by themselves establish NP differs from coNP; that conclusion requires ruling out every polynomially bounded Cook–Reckhow proof system.

scenarios.title: Prove the Hamiltonian quantum PCP conjecture
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: A gap-amplification/completeness result can be a major advance without changing a total-language class inclusion.

scenarios.title: Separate promise-QMA from promise-QCMA without a total-language witness
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: A promise-problem witness does not automatically produce a total language in QMA outside QCMA. The corresponding total-language scenario is advance-08.

scenarios.title: A new separation relative to an oracle
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: The scorer fixes unrelativized classes. Even a major new oracle separation does not prove their unrelativized noninclusion. The classical-oracle QMA/QCMA problem was already solved before the cutoff.

scenarios.title: A superlinear or fixed-exponent Boolean circuit lower bound for an explicit NP language
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: Ruling out n^1.01-size circuits leaves n^2-size circuits possible and does not give NP not contained in P/poly. Likewise fixed-depth threshold bounds do not settle NEXP versus TC0.

scenarios.title: Optimal explicit Ramsey graph constructions
scenarios.why_not_guaranteed: A construction for one combinatorial object need not derandomize all BPP languages or resolve any roster pair. Whole-class consequences would need their own proof.

gaps: Individual algorithms versus whole complexity classes
Fixed resource exponents and fine-grained complexity
Proof systems, relativization and barrier results
A finite sample cannot support a claim to cover the 50 most likely advances without a separately elicited and versioned forecast distribution.

roster_recommendation.accepted_choice: Use the agreed 50-class roster, with nonuniform AC0/ACC0/TC0/NC1 and uniform NC. NISZK is omitted.
roster_recommendation.benefit: The nonuniform convention represents central circuit-lower-bound questions directly. P/poly and NP/poly retain arbitrary advice, including undecidable languages.
roster_recommendation.tradeoff: Dropping NISZK omits a recognized zero-knowledge question; adding it back alone would not repair the promise-language distinction. E and NE retain some padding structure but do not capture most quantitative exponential-time advances.
possible_future_tracks: Fixed-exponent circuit, time and proof-size targets
